title: The Quiet Kitchen
theme: What your parents' silence about money taught you
lyrics:
[Intro]
Mm, the fridge is humming low

[Verse 1]
Mama folded the envelope in half
Papa set his keys down soft beside the door
Nobody said the word, they just went quiet
And the kitchen light stayed on a little more
I learned to read a silence like a bill
Slid under a door I couldn't see
I kept my face still at the dinner table
So nobody would have to speak for me

[Pre-Chorus]
And I grew up hearing what got left unsaid
Like a radio playing somewhere down the hall

[Chorus]
We never talked about the money
So I learned to hold it quiet
Now I count it in the dark
And I still can't say it out loud

[Verse 2]
I bought a lunch box from a thrift store shelf
It had a dent right where my name should go
I carry it like it's something I should hide
But it's just a box I eat my lunch from, though
My phone screen cracked the week the rent came due
I didn't call, I let the message sit
I thought that was the way the grown folks handle it
But quiet is a weight that you can't quit

[Pre-Chorus]
And I grew up hearing what got left unsaid
Like a radio playing somewhere down the hall

[Chorus]
We never talked about the money
So I learned to hold it quiet
Now I count it in the dark
And I still can't say it out loud

[Bridge]
What if the silence was just fear
Dressed up in its Sunday clothes
What if the first word I say
Is the one that lets the room exhale
What if I'm the kitchen light
That finally stays on for the ones who come after

[Final Chorus]
We never talked about the money
So I learned to hold it quiet
Now I count it in the dark
And I'm learning how to say it out loud

[Outro]
Say it soft
Say it anyway
Say it soft
The kitchen light is on

title: First One Off the Line
theme: Being the first in your family to break a pattern, and carrying that weight without letting it crush you
lyrics:
[Intro]
(soft tape hiss, a porch light hum)

[Verse 1]
Dad counted coins in a mason jar,
Mom folded envelopes under a book,
Nobody said the word debt out loud,
Just the sound of a bill through the door.

[Pre-Chorus]
I got a phone with a cracked screen glow,
Every alert sounds like a no,
I'm learning words they never taught me,
Reading slow to find where I stand.

[Chorus]
I'm the first one breaking the line,
Carrying a name I didn't sign,
So I'll leave the porch light on tonight,
Let the next one walk in without the fight.

[Verse 2]
Night shift, lunch in a plastic tray,
I do the math before I eat the meal,
Mama calls, asks if I've eaten,
I say yes, and it's half true, half real.
I wrote a list of everything I owe,
Then cried in the car where no one would know,
Sat with the engine ticking, counting breaths,
Then I walked up the steps and held the rest.

[Pre-Chorus]
I'm not ashamed of where I came from,
I'm just tired of flinching at the mail,
Opening each envelope slow,
Letting the shake turn into a plan.

[Chorus]
I'm the first one breaking the line,
Carrying a name I didn't sign,
So I'll leave the porch light on tonight,
Let the next one walk in without the fight.

[Bridge]
Is it failing if you're the first to try?
Or the first one brave enough to ask why?
A pattern is just a habit someone had to hold,
You can set it down and still be whole.

[Final Chorus]
I'm the first one breaking the line,
Carrying a name I didn't sign,
So I'll leave the porch light on tonight,
Let the next one walk in without the fight.

[Outro]
Line bends, the door swings wide,
I'm the first, and I'm walking inside.

title: Small Warm Light
theme: Buying comfort while hurting, and forgiving yourself for it
lyrics:
[Intro]

[Verse 1]
Paper bag warm on the seat beside me
Radio low and the lot still wet
Phone screen cracked across the same bad number
I swore I'd wait, then I was pulling in

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the math, I know the hour
I know the sound a bill makes at the door
But my hands were tired and the bag was hot
So I let the small things in before

[Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Verse 2]
Hoodie two sizes too big for grief
Receipts folded small inside my coat
A candle from the drugstore, lit for no one
Whispering the sorry I still owe

[Pre-Chorus]
I know the math, I know the hour
I know the sound a bill makes at the door
But the night was long and the window was black
So I let the warm things in, and I'm back

[Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Bridge]
Who taught us comfort was a crime?
Hurt people reach for what is near
The bag was never the whole story
The shame was heavier than the paper
So ask what the hurt was asking for
And meet it with a kinder hand tomorrow

[Final Chorus]
I bought myself a little light
To sit with me when the rooms went dark
It cost me more than the bag would say
And I can forgive the one who paid

[Outro]
Porch light on, the door unlocked
Tomorrow I can start again
A little light, a little rest
I'm allowed to be both the hurt and the healing
